notes: Maria Leptin | EMBO Science Journalism Fellowships is a science journalism scheme (EMBO, embo.org), not a degree or research programme. Journalists arrange funded placements (sabbaticals) at one or more research institutions of their own choosing, and researchers transition into journalism via placements in media newsrooms - no host institution or supervising professor is attached to the award. Namesake Professor Maria Leptin is the private donor, not a supervisor. Official EMBO contacts are staff (Marina Giampietro, Head of Communications; Guillaume Parodi, Community Engagement Officer), not professors. Analogous to a central Fulbright-style scheme: outcome not_applicable. Verified live at https://www.embo.org/funding/fellowships-grants-and-career-support/maria-leptin-embo-science-journalism-fellowships - 'The scheme supports science journalism by providing: Journalists with funded placements (sabbaticals) at one or more research institutions...'

UM NL Global Studies Scholarship (Maastricht University) is a full-coverage entrance scholarship for one admitted bachelor's student in the three-year Global Studies bachelor's programme. It is awarded on admission application and scholarship application ranking (tuition at cost plus EUR 20,150 living stipend per year, 2027-2028), with no supervising professor, research group, or named programme faculty attached to the award. Bachelor's programmes have no supervisor structure. Official page verified live at https://www.maastrichtuniversity.nl/studeren/toelating-inschrijving/financing-your-studies/scholarships/um-nl-global-studies - scholarship is awarded to 'a bachelor student who has been admitted to its Global Studies bachelor's programme'; no faculty names or supervisor contacts published on the scholarship page.

Latvian State Scholarship for Foreign Students is a national government scheme administered by the State Education Development Agency (VIAA) through studyinlatvia.lv / scholarships.viaa.gov.lv. It pays a monthly stipend (EUR 500 bachelor/master, EUR 700 doctoral) to students from 30+ partner countries enrolled at any Latvian HEI of their choice; no institution or supervising professor is attached to the scheme itself. Applicants obtain a confirmation letter from a designated HEI contact person, but these are administrative contacts, not scholarship supervisors. Analogous to MEXT/GKS-style national schemes: outcome not_applicable. Verified live at https://studyinlatvia.lv/scholarships - 'An applicant must choose a study programme at a Latvian HEI prior to the application for the scholarship' and 'All applications will be evaluated and the final decision on granting scholarships will be made by the evaluation committee of VIAA.'

University of Manitoba International Excellence Entrance Scholarship is a bachelor's entrance award (one at $25,000, two at $10,000) for international high school graduates entering University 1 or any faculty/college/school with a direct-entry option. Selection is by the awards office (Financial Aid and Awards, awards@umanitoba.ca) based on admission average (90% for the top award) and leadership/community involvement, with one recommendation from a teacher or principal. No supervising professor or programme faculty is tied to the scholarship; first-year entrance awards have no supervisor structure. Official page verified live at https://umanitoba.ca/financial-aid-and-awards/entrance-awards/international-excellence-entrance-scholarship - 'Short-listed applicants will be ranked in a level of first, second and third place based on the results from the award application and the admissions application.' Contact listed is the Financial Aid and Awards office, not a professor.

Killam Predoctoral Scholarship Level 2 (Doctoral) at Dalhousie University is a university-wide doctoral scholarship supported by the Killam Trusts, 'awarded competitively to outstanding doctoral students across all disciplines, including the sciences, engineering, humanities, and social sciences'. Applications go through the Faculty of Graduate Studies (or automatic consideration via Tri-agency CGRS-D), with Faculty-level review then an institutional Killam Predoctoral Scholarship Review Committee. No specific supervisor, lab, or department is attached to the scholarship; recipients identify their own supervisor through the separate 'Find your supervisor' process. Official page verified live at https://www.dal.ca/faculty/gradstudies/finance-your-studies/scholarships-bursaries/killam-master-doctoral.html - scholarship is open to students 'pursuing a full time doctoral (PhD) degree at Dalhousie University'; page text references a recipient's supervisor generically ('discuss potential impacts to overall funding packages with their supervisor and/or graduate coordinator') but names no professor.

Dalhousie Research Excellence Scholarship (DRES) is a university-wide doctoral entrance scholarship (est. 2024) for exceptional new PhD students at Dalhousie, $35,000/year for up to four years ($28,000 from Graduate Studies plus $7,000 from the supervisor and/or programme of study). It is not tied to any named supervisor, lab, or department; adjudication is Faculty-level review plus an institutional review committee, with application via the Faculty of Graduate Studies Scholarship Management Platform or automatic consideration via CGRS-D. The $7,000 supervisor contribution refers to the recipient's own supervisor chosen after admission, not a professor attached to the award. Official page verified live at https://www.dal.ca/faculty/gradstudies/finance-your-studies/scholarships-bursaries/research-excellence-scholarship.html - 'the remaining $7000 will be provided by your supervisor and/or program of study'; no professor names published.

National Humanities Center Residential Fellowship is offered by the NHC, a private nonprofit independent institute for advanced study in the humanities (not a university degree programme). Fellows are established scholars (PhD or terminal degree at least five years prior, with a published monograph or equivalent) who pursue individual, largely single-author projects in residence, supported by stipend, library, and an intellectual community. There is no supervising professor, programme faculty, or research group tied to the fellowship; selection is by fellowship competition based on the project proposal. NHC leadership (President and Director Blair LM Kelley; VP for Scholarly Programs Martha Kelly) are administrative staff, not supervisors. Official page verified live at https://nationalhumanitiescenter.org/residential-fellowships - 'Fellowships offer scholars the time, space, and support they need to pursue their work'; 'The National Humanities Center is a private, nonprofit organization, and the only independent institute dedicated exclusively to advanced study in all areas of the humanities.'
